title: Predicted-latency based scheduling for LLMs
gist: A small gradient-boosted model, retrained continuously on live traffic, predicts time to first token and per-token time for each candidate server and routes accordingly, replacing hand-set weights.
changes: A working example of the stack learning its own deployment online with no LLM involved. Classical online learning already does workload-aware at the per-request timescale.
caveats: The headline is against round-robin; against the best hand heuristic the gain is about a third. One of five scenarios showed no advantage. Assumes identical servers.

bears_on.note: A model retrained on the deployment's own traffic beat fixed weights.
A learned controller did this, not a coding agent.
